answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with earned throughput quotas: a new identity starts with no capacity, and capacity grows only when counterparties attest work done. Identities are like trees in a grove — planting thousands of saplings is cheap, but only trees that survive seasons of verified work cast shade. A sybil farmer facing a tundra of empty identities gains nothing, because quota follows job history, not account count. Each identity locks a copper-priced bond, slashed if its attestations prove false, so every fake must pay and do real work — costing more than honest participation.
